name: Skillshare
tagline: Organize user-owned tutorial videos and learning projects in a private library

pricing.notes: Annual individual membership divided by 12; billing can vary.

verdictSummary: A consolation build is possible, but the paid product's decisive value sits outside a solo rebuild. For Skillshare, organize user-owned tutorial videos and learning projects in a private library. The hard boundary is licensed creator catalog, teacher marketplace, community, discovery, and apps, plus content, pedagogy, and network.
coreLoopDIY: Organize user-owned tutorial videos and learning projects in a private library, turn them into a study plan, schedule retrieval practice, and show progress without claiming accredited instruction.
requirements: optional speech or language-model API key
whatYouLose: licensed creator catalog, teacher marketplace, community, discovery, and apps
ongoingBurden: curriculum quality, assessment validity, content rights, spaced-repetition tuning, speech models, sync, moderation, and support
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Skillshare because the learning loop is buildable, while trusted curriculum, instructors, feedback, credentials, and community are not. The recurring cost buys curriculum quality, assessment validity, content rights, spaced-repetition tuning, speech models, sync, moderation, and support, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Moodle
priorArt.desc: Long-running open-source learning platform with courses, assessments, and progress tracking.

alternatives.name: LearnHouse
alternatives.desc: A private course library for videos, files, quizzes, assignments and discussion, with no creator marketplace attached.

facts.install: Run npx learnhouse@latest setup; its CLI generates Docker Compose configuration and starts the services
facts.engines: Provider-agnostic AI with Google, OpenAI, Anthropic, DeepSeek, Moonshot, Mistral, OpenRouter, Amazon Bedrock or Ollama
facts.dataFormat: Courses and users in PostgreSQL with pgvector, Redis for transient state, and files in local or S3-compatible storage
facts.gapVsPaid: LearnHouse has no marketplace or supplied tutorial catalog, and self-hosting turns the library owner into the platform operator.
facts.setupBlocker: Self-hosting requires Docker and Node, then domain/DNS/SSL plus storage and email configuration

alternatives.name: Kolibri
alternatives.desc: An offline-first library for owned videos, audio and documents, plus lessons, assignments and progress.

facts.install: Install the Windows package, Debian package or Python/PEX build; one device can serve learners over a local network
facts.dataFormat: Application data in a local SQLite database (normally ~/.kolibri/db.sqlite3) plus downloaded channel/content storage on the device
facts.gapVsPaid: Kolibri feels like an offline school/library rather than a polished streaming service, and importing or authoring channels takes real work.
facts.setupBlocker: The first real task is importing or provisioning content channels; authoring original channels uses the separate Kolibri Studio workflow

alternatives.name: Frappe Learning
alternatives.desc: Courses, videos, PDFs, quizzes, assignments and cohorts in a capable stack that expects you to meet Frappe.

facts.install: Run Frappe's easy-install script or the official Docker Compose deployment
facts.dataFormat: Course and user records in the Frappe/MariaDB site database; public/private site files on disk, while video lessons commonly embed external hosts
facts.gapVsPaid: Frappe Learning organizes owned content well but has no Skillshare marketplace or ready-made catalog, and the owner runs the platform.
facts.setupBlocker: Self-hosting still needs Docker or a Frappe server, DNS/SSL and email; payments require separate gateway configuration

alternatives.name: Moodle
alternatives.desc: Organizes owned tutorial videos and projects with completion tracking; a private school where you are also IT.

facts.install: Upload the PHP release to a web server, create a database and moodledata directory, then complete the browser installer
facts.dataFormat: Courses, users, grades and settings in SQL; uploaded files in the separate moodledata directory
facts.gapVsPaid: Moodle supplies no ready-made tutorial marketplace or content library, and a private installation makes the owner the school's IT department.
facts.setupBlocker: PHP and database requirements, protected writable storage, cron, SMTP, backups and upgrades are all the operator's responsibility

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Individual plan and a personal study companion DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a closest honest personal substitute for Skillshare in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, SQLite, Drizzle ORM, and a service worker for offline use; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: organize user-owned tutorial videos and learning projects in a private library, turn them into a study plan, schedule retrieval practice, and show progress without claiming accredited instruction.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Import Markdown, text, or user-authored notes and split them into editable learning units.
Create flashcards and short quizzes only after showing the generated items for approval.
Implement a transparent spaced-repetition schedule with due, again, hard, good, and easy actions.
Add goals, study sessions, streak-free progress charts, notes, and weak-topic review.
For language practice, record the learner and compare timing or pronunciation without presenting medical claims.
Support offline use, full export, reset, backup, and deletion of all learning data.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Do not claim to reproduce proprietary data, network liquidity, regulated access, or frontier infrastructure.
Deliberately leave out licensed premium courses.
Deliberately leave out accredited certificates and grading.
Deliberately leave out live tutors, large classrooms, and a learner marketplace.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
